content: The references provided are a list of studies, reports, and clinical trials related to HIV treatment, antiretroviral therapy (ART), drug resistance, and clinical outcomes. 1. Back D, Khoo S, Marzolini C, et al. This reference discusses drug interactions in HIV treatment, providing a comprehensive resource for understanding how antiretroviral drugs interact with other medications. The information is accessible via an online platform and was last accessed on June 1, 2021. 2. Chouraya C, Ashburn K, Khumalo P, et al. This study examines the association between specific antiretroviral drug regimens and viral suppression in HIV-positive children undergoing therapy in Eswatini. Published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal in 2019, it highlights the effectiveness of ART in pediatric populations. 3. FDA approval for pediatric HIV treatment. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced the approval of a new drug specifically designed to treat infants and children with HIV. This milestone was accessed online on June 1, 2021. 4. Tivicay (Dolutegravir). This reference provides detailed information about the antiretroviral drug Dolutegravir, including its clinical applications and safety profile. The data was retrieved from an official source on June 1, 2021. 5. Kobbe R, Schalkwijk S, Dunay G, et al. This study investigates the presence of Dolutegravir in breast milk and its pharmacokinetics in both maternal and infant plasma during breastfeeding. Published in AIDS in 2016, it provides critical insights into the safety of Dolutegravir for breastfeeding mothers and their infants. 6. Iyer SS, Pry J, Nyirenda G, et al. This research focuses on the impact of Dolutegravir on viral load suppression among pediatric patients receiving care in Zambia. The findings were presented at the 28th Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections (CROI) in 2021. 7. Bacha J, Mayalla B, Jiwa N, et al. This study explores the rollout of Dolutegravir for children and adolescents living with HIV in Mbeya, Tanzania. It identifies trends, gaps, and challenges in implementing this treatment strategy. 8. Paton N, Musazzi J, Kityo CM, et al. The NADIA trial evaluates the outcomes of nucleosides and Darunavir/Dolutegravir regimens in African populations over 48 weeks. The study provides evidence for optimizing second-line ART in resource-limited settings. 9. Hill A, Mitchell N, Hughes S, et al. A meta-analysis of 13 randomized trials involving 7,340 patients assesses the efficacy and safety of Dolutegravir, particularly in relation to current HIV RNA suppression levels. 10. Gregson J, Tang M, Ndembi N, et al. This multicenter retrospective cohort study examines global drug resistance patterns following the failure of WHO-recommended first-line ART regimens for adult HIV-1 infection. 11. WHO Think-Tank Meeting on ART Optimization. A report from a meeting held on March 12, 2020, discusses strategies for optimizing antiretroviral therapy, with a focus on public health approaches in resource-limited settings. 12. WHO HIVResNet Meeting Report. This report summarizes discussions from a meeting in Johannesburg, South Africa, on October 21, 2018, addressing HIV drug resistance and its implications for treatment programs. 13. Consolidated Guidelines on HIV Prevention and Treatment. The WHO provides comprehensive guidelines on HIV prevention, testing, treatment, service delivery, and monitoring, emphasizing a public health approach. 14. Vitoria M, Vella S, Ford N. This article discusses the challenges and strategies for scaling up ART in resource-limited settings, emphasizing the need for adaptable guidance to meet local needs. 15. Aboud M, Brites C, Lu H, et al. The DAWNING trial compares Dolutegravir with Lopinavir/Ritonavir in second-line ART, focusing on outcomes based on WHO-recommended NRTI backbones. 16. Vitoria M, Hill AM, Ford NP, et al. This publication explores the selection of antiretroviral drugs for treatment scale-up in public health programs, identifying knowledge gaps and future research priorities. 17. Vitoria M, Ford N, Clayden P, et al. A WHO Think Tank report examines the potential for recommending new antiretroviral drugs in lowand middle-income countries, based on emerging evidence. 18. The PHIA Project. This online resource provides data on population-based HIV impact assessments, offering insights into the effectiveness of national HIV programs. 19. Pediatric Antiretroviral Drug Optimization (PADO) Meeting 4. This meeting report focuses on optimizing ART for children, addressing gaps in drug formulations and delivery. 20. Rabie H, Denti P, Lee J, et al. This study evaluates the pharmacokinetics and clinical outcomes of Lopinavir-Ritonavir super-boosting in young children on Rifampicin-based tuberculosis therapy. 21. Sunpath H, Winterheimer P, Cohen S, et al. This research investigates the use of double-dose Lopinavir-Ritonavir in combination with Rifampicin-based TB treatment in South Africa. 22. Decloedt EH, McIlleron H, Smith P, et al. The pharmacokinetics of Lopinavir in HIV-infected adults receiving adjusted doses with Rifampin are analyzed in this study. 23. Ebrahim I, Maartens G, Smythe W, et al. This study examines the safety and pharmacokinetics of adjusted Darunavir/Ritonavir with Rifampin in people living with HIV. 24. Burger D, Agarwala S, Child M, et al. The effects of Rifampin on the pharmacokinetics of Atazanavir with Ritonavir in healthy volunteers are explored in this research. 25. Eholie SP, Moh R, Benalycherif A, et al. This prospective cohort study evaluates an intensive adherence intervention for patients with second-line ART failure in West Africa. 26. Pozniak A, Opravil M, Beatty G, et al. The POWER 1 and 2 studies assess the impact of baseline viral susceptibility on responses to Darunavir/Ritonavir in treatment-experienced patients. 27. Antiretroviral Therapy for HIV in Adults and Adolescents. WHO guidelines provide recommendations for ART in adults and adolescents, emphasizing a public health approach. 28. Ajose O, Mookerjee S, Mills EJ, et al. A systematic review and meta-analysis of treatment outcomes for patients on second-line ART in resource-limited settings. 29. Steigbigel RT, Cooper DA, Kumar PN, et al. The efficacy and safety of Raltegravir with optimized background therapy for resistant HIV-1 infection are evaluated in this study. 30. Schiller DS, Youssef-Bessler M. This article reviews Etravirine, a second-generation NNRTI effective against NNRTI-resistant HIV strains. 31. Gatell JM, Katlama C, Grinsztejn B, et al. Long-term efficacy and safety of Raltegravir in patients with limited treatment options are reported in a Phase II study. 32. Steigbigel RT, Cooper DA, Teppler H, et al. The BENCHMRK trials provide long-term data on Raltegravir combined with optimized background therapy in treatment-experienced patients. 33. Katlama C, Clotet B, Mills A, et al. The DUET trials evaluate the efficacy and safety of Etravirine in treatment-experienced HIV-1-infected patients. 34. Fagard C, Colin C, Charpentier C, et al. The ANRS 139 TRIO trial reports long-term outcomes of Raltegravir, Etravirine, and Darunavir/Ritonavir in treatment-experienced patients. 35. Consolidated Guidelines on Antiretroviral Drugs. WHO guidelines provide recommendations for the use of ART in treating and preventing HIV infection. 36. Cahn P, Pozniak AL, Mingrone H, et al. The SAILING study compares Dolutegravir with Raltegravir in integrase-inhibitor-naive adults with HIV. 37. Eron JJ, Cooper DA, Steigbigel RT, et al. The BENCHMRK studies report final results on the efficacy and safety of Raltegravir for HIV treatment over five years. 38. Capetti A, Meraviglia P, Landonio S, et al. The SALIR-E study provides four years of data on Raltegravir-based salvage therapy in treatment-experienced patients. 39. Gazzola L, Cicconi P, Ripamonti D, et al. This study evaluates the efficacy and safety of Darunavir/Ritonavir plus Etravirine in treatment-experienced patients. 40. Arathoon E, Bhorat A, Silaghi R, et al. A Phase IV trial examines Etravirine with other antiretrovirals in treatment-experienced adults. 41. Castagna A, Maggiolo F, Penco G, et al. The VIKING-3 study evaluates Dolutegravir in patients with resistance to Raltegravir and/or Elvitegravir. 42. Vingerhoets J, Calvez V, Flandre P, et al. An observational study assesses the efficacy of Etravirine combined with Darunavir or other Ritonavir-boosted protease inhibitors. 43. Lazarus E, Nicol S, Frigati L, et al. A scoping review of secondand third-line ART for children and adolescents highlights gaps in treatment options. 44. Fox Z, Dragsted UB, Gerstoft J, et al. The COLATE trial evaluates the continuation versus discontinuation of Lamivudine in individuals failing a Lamivudine-containing regimen. 45. Prado JG, Parkin NT, Clotet B, et al. This study examines the evolution of HIV-1 fitness in treatment-experienced patients with sustained CD4+ T-cell counts but persistent virologic failure. 46. Tashima K, Smeaton L, Andrade A, et al. The ACTG OPTIONS study demonstrates that omitting NRTIs from ART regimens is not inferior to adding NRTIs in treatment-experienced patients. 47. Grinsztejn B, Hughes MD, Ritz J, et al. The ACTG A5288 study evaluates third-line ART strategies in lowand middle-income countries. 48. Forecasts of Antiretroviral Medicines Demand. WHO provides global and regional demand forecasts for ART in lowand middle-income countries from 2014 to 2018. 49. Pediatric ARV Drug Optimization 2. A WHO meeting report addresses the optimization of ART for children, focusing on drug formulations and delivery. 50. Harrigan R. This article discusses the clinical measurement of viral load in HIV management. 51. Gilks C, Walker A, Munderi P, et al. A single CD4 test with a 250 cells/mm³ threshold predicts viral suppression in adults failing first-line therapy. 52. Katirayi L, Ochuka B, Mafaune H, et al. A qualitative study explores caregivers' and community members' perspectives on point-of-care early infant diagnosis. 53. Broyles LN, Boeras D, Luo R, et al. A review of the viral load monitoring algorithm in people living with HIV on ART informs WHO guidelines. 54. Cahn P, Madero JS, Arribas JR, et al. The GEMINI trials compare Dolutegravir plus Lamivudine with Dolutegravir plus Tenofovir Disoproxil Fumarate and Emtricitabine in ART-naive adults. 55. Venter WDF, Moorhouse M, Sokhela S, et al. This study evaluates Dolutegravir with two different prodrugs of Tenofovir for HIV treatment. 56. Group NAS, Kouanfack C, Mpoudi-Etame M, et al. A study compares Dolutegravir-based and low-dose Efavirenz-based regimens for HIV-1 treatment. 57. Sax PE, Pozniak A, Montes ML, et al. A Phase III trial compares coformulated Bictegravir, Emtricitabine, and Tenofovir Alafenamide with Dolutegravir-based regimens for initial HIV treatment. 58. Rossetti B, Baldin G, Sterrantino G, et al. A multicenter cohort study evaluates Dolutegravir-based regimens in advanced HIV-infected naive patients. 59. Clotet B, Feinberg J, van Lunzen J, et al. The FLAMINGO study compares once-daily Dolutegravir with Darunavir plus Ritonavir in ART-naive adults. 60. ARROW Trial Team. A five-year trial evaluates routine versus clinically driven laboratory monitoring and first-line ART strategies in African children with HIV. 61. Violari A, Lindsey JC, Hughes MD, et al. A study compares Nevirapine with Ritonavir-boosted Lopinavir for HIV-infected children. 62. Gregson J, Tang M, Ndembi N, et al. A global study examines drug resistance following the failure of WHO-recommended first-line ART regimens.
